newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power steady amid NIMO nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power steady amid NIMO nuke outage.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. ended mostly steady Wednesday against Tuesday following news of an unplanned shutdown of a nuclear power unit operated by Niagara Mohawk Power Corp (NIMO).
"It helped a little," a Houston marketer said, adding bids for spot power did not in general rise with higher offers.
The Nine Mile Point nuclear unit 1 in Scriba, N.Y., which tripped off line late Tuesday due to a generator problem, was expected to return to service by this weekend.
The adjoining 1,137 megawatt Nine Mile Point unit 2 was approaching full output after completing its refueling outage that began in late September.
"I don't think there's any net change (in terms of generation)," said one New York trader.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday delivery was assessed at $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Tuesday's range.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Thursday was again pegged in the $13.50-$14.50.
Electricity in the western NYPP district for the balance of November was offered near $24.00.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday was notationally valued higher at $29.00-$31.00, up from Tuesday's $27.00-$29.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Thursday electricity in eastern NYPP was still pegged at $16.00-$18.00.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at the Northeast Utilities border was again discussed in the $31.00-$33.00 range, but today's offers were heard as high as $34.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was again quoted at $18.00-$19.50.
NEPOOL and NYPP spot prices could rise on outlook of an Arctic blast descending into the Northeast by the weekend, market sources said.

The New York Power Authority was scheduled to restore a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission power line from Quebec to New York after shutting two segments of the line last weekend for seasonal maintenance.
